sections.title: Copper Cabling & Standards
sections.content:
Twisted-pair copper is the workhorse of the LAN. Twisting reduces crosstalk and EMI.
Category | Max speed | Max distance | Notes
Cat 5e | 1 Gbps | 100 m | Minimum for modern Gigabit
Cat 6 | 1 Gbps (10G to 55 m) | 100 m / 55 m | Tighter twist, less crosstalk
Cat 6a | 10 Gbps | 100 m | Shielded options; 10G full distance
Cat 7 | 10 Gbps | 100 m | Fully shielded (S/FTP), GG45
Cat 8 | 25-40 Gbps | 30 m | Data center short runs
The 100-meter rule: copper Ethernet is limited to ~100 m (90 m horizontal + 10 m patch). Beyond that, use fiber.
Shielding: UTP (unshielded) is cheapest and common; STP/FTP (shielded) resists interference in noisy environments.
Termination standards: T568A and T568B define the pin-out. Straight-through (same standard both ends) connects unlike devices; a crossover (A on one end, B on the other) connects like devices — though Auto-MDIX now handles this automatically.
Plenum-rated cable (CMP) has fire-resistant, low-smoke jacketing required in air-handling spaces.
exam_tips: Copper Ethernet max run = 100 meters. Need farther = fiber.
Cat 6a is the common choice for 10 Gbps over the full 100 m.
Plenum (CMP) cable is required in air-handling spaces for fire safety.

sections.title: Fiber Optic Cabling
sections.content:
Fiber carries light, immune to EMI, with huge distance and bandwidth.
Single-mode (SMF) — tiny 9-micron core, laser light, very long distance (km+), yellow jacket. Long-haul, campus/WAN.
Multimode (MMF) — larger 50/62.5-micron core, LED/VCSEL, shorter distance (up to ~550 m), aqua/orange jacket. Within buildings/data centers. OM3/OM4/OM5 grades.
Connectors: LC (small form, duplex, most common today), SC (square, push-pull), ST (round bayonet, older), MPO/MTP (multi-fiber ribbon for high density).
Transceivers (pluggable optics):
SFP — 1 Gbps.
SFP+ — 10 Gbps.
QSFP / QSFP+ — 40 Gbps (quad).
QSFP28 — 100 Gbps.
Match the transceiver to the fiber type and wavelength on BOTH ends.
exam_tips: Single-mode = long distance (laser, small core); multimode = shorter runs (LED, larger core).
LC is the most common modern fiber connector; MPO/MTP is for high-density ribbon.

sections.title: Transceivers, Media Converters & Distribution
sections.content:
Media converter — bridges two media types (e.g., copper to fiber) to extend a link beyond copper's 100 m.
Transceiver form factors are hot-swappable; 'BiDi' optics send/receive on one strand using two wavelengths.
Structured cabling components:
MDF (Main Distribution Frame) — the building's primary wiring hub.
IDF (Intermediate Distribution Frame) — floor/wing closets that connect back to the MDF.
Patch panel — terminates permanent cable runs; patch cables jumper to switches.
66/110 blocks — punch-down termination (110 is modern data; 66 is legacy voice).
Demarcation point (demarc) — where the ISP's responsibility ends and yours begins.
exam_tips: Use a media converter (or fiber) when a run exceeds copper's 100 m limit.
MDF = main hub; IDF = intermediate closet that links back to the MDF.
The demarc is the ISP/customer responsibility boundary.

concept_cards.hook: The maximum run for twisted-pair copper Ethernet (90 m horizontal + 10 m patch). Beyond it, signal degrades — use fiber.
Fiber with a ~9-micron core carrying laser light over very long distances (kilometers); yellow jacket, used for WAN/long-haul.
Fiber with a 50/62.5-micron core carrying LED/VCSEL light over shorter distances (up to ~550 m); aqua/orange jacket, used inside buildings.
Hot-swappable fiber transceiver form factors: SFP=1 Gbps, SFP+=10 Gbps, QSFP28=100 Gbps. Must match the fiber and wavelength on both ends.
Cable with fire-resistant, low-smoke jacketing required by code in air-handling (plenum) spaces like drop ceilings.
Straight-through (same T568 standard both ends) connects unlike devices; crossover (A/B) connects like devices. Auto-MDIX now negotiates this automatically.
A device that converts between media types (e.g., copper to fiber) to extend a link past copper's distance limit.
The physical point where the service provider's network ends and the customer's network begins; the responsibility boundary.

practice_questions.q: What is the maximum run length for twisted-pair copper Ethernet?
practice_questions.explanation: Copper Ethernet is limited to about 100 m (90 m horizontal + 10 m patch); beyond that use fiber.

practice_questions.q: Which fiber type uses a laser and a small core for very long distances?
practice_questions.explanation: Single-mode fiber has a ~9-micron core and uses laser light for kilometer-plus distances.

practice_questions.q: Which transceiver form factor supports 100 Gbps?
A cable run must pass through an air-handling ceiling space. Which cable is required?
practice_questions.explanation: Plenum spaces require fire-resistant, low-smoke plenum-rated (CMP) cable by code.
